To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) difficulty levels are perceived as a source of boredom, 2) engagement is perceived as a source that can be used to modulate difficulty levels, 3) boredom and anxiety can be detected from physiological signals.

boredom, engagement and anxiety were found to be the most relevant emotions to be considered for adaptation to difficulty, and that physiological data were able to provide a good indication of the emotional state of players.

playing at different difficulty level gives rise to different emotional state, playing at the same difficulty level several times elicits a boredom state, and the emotional state of the player can be assessed from physiological signals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a system that can be used by game developers to assess player’s emotions and adapt the level of game difficulty to keep the player engaged.
the development of a system for emotion recognition based on physiological measures that can be used to adapt the game difficulty and maintain the players’ engagement.

the development of a system that can recognize the emotional states of the players, and adapt the difficulty of the game in order to keep them in the state of engagement, which is the state in which players are the most likely to learn and enjoy the game.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the difficulty level of a game has an influence on the players’ emotions and that the emotion recognition of boredom, anxiety and engagement can be used to modulate difficulty in a game.
boredom is an important indicator of difficulty in games.
the proposed emotion recognition approach could be useful for game designers to adapt the game to the player's emotional state and thus to keep the player engaged.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
boredom, engagement and anxiety are good candidates to be used as indicators for difficulty adaptation.
the game difficulty can be modulated to maintain the player's engagement and prevent boredom.
the game difficulty level has an effect on the emotional state of a player and that this effect can be assessed from physiological data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
physiological measures are able to discriminate different emotional classes, which could be used to modulate game difficulty.
the use of emotion recognition to adapt game difficulty can be a viable solution to maintain engagement of the players.
the use of physiological signals can be a useful complement to the self-report questionnaires to detect emotional states and to adapt difficulty in a game.
